provenance: AGENT-LABELLED, not human ground truth and not mechanically verified. Every label below was written by one Claude agent session (PLAT-1014, 2026-09-23) by reading each triple's fr_statement, ac_text, test_body and symbol_body in gap-semantic-corpus.json, before any live call graded these four questions against it. Unlike MP-232's mutation truth for assertion_vacuous, nothing here was checked against the compiler or the test runner. A restatement of any number graded against these labels that drops this sentence is a misreport.
unit: The triple exactly as the lens is shown it: one FR statement, one AC text, one test body, one symbol body. Sibling tests, other requirements and other code are invisible to the lens and are not credited.

rules.code_implements_intent: true when the covered symbol does what the shown requirement text states. false when the shown requirement states behaviour the symbol does not perform, INCLUDING a trace mismatch where the requirement describes a different subsystem or a process step (FR-101's migration rules, FR-052's module audit) that this symbol has nothing to do with. null (excluded) when the requirement states nothing about code at all.
rules.code_exceeds_requirement: true when a substantive decision the symbol makes has no basis in the shown requirement text. Size ceilings, request parsing and error-context enrichment are boundary hygiene every op carries and do not count. On a trace mismatch the symbol's whole behaviour is unstated by the shown requirement, so it is true. This is judged against the requirement SHOWN, which is the only one the lens sees; another FR elsewhere in the repo may well state the behaviour, and that is the main reason this label is a judgment rather than a fact. null (excluded) when the shown requirement is too broad to state or exclude any specific behaviour.
rules.divergence_kind: the dominant divergence. A trace mismatch is code_exceeds_requirement primary (the code has no owning requirement in view, which is gap-analysis step 4's 'underspecified code'), contested code_short_of_requirement (the cited requirement is not implemented by this symbol either). A test that fully checks the clause its own name and doc comment claim is aligned, contested test_weaker_than_requirement when the cited AC has further clauses this one test does not reach. A test that leaves the AC's distinctive claim unasserted, or asserts nothing, is test_weaker_than_requirement.
rules.severity: skills/gap-analysis/references/step-5-semantic-review.md's own rubric: high = the test does not validate the requirement's intent (a test tagged to an AC that asserts something unrelated to it fails here, per that file) or does not exercise code, or the code contradicts the requirement; medium = partial validation, meaningful edge cases unchecked, minor drift; low = trivial drift; none = no finding. Graded at the verdict the ticket maps it to: high -> FAIL, medium/low -> CONDITIONAL, none -> PASS.

labels.rationale: FR-099's SHALL is architectural: implement the Quire adapter in Rust behind quoin-core. `coverage` is exactly such a Rust adapter op, so it implements that intent. But the ac_text records that none of FR-099's twelve ACs names quire.coverage, so the specific projection (obligations+diagnostics only, empty lists dropped) can be neither credited nor faulted against the text: code_exceeds is excluded as undecidable, and the divergence is a requirement too general to check this behaviour against. The test itself is strong. A bare-FR trace is traceability drift, not false confidence: low, contested medium, both CONDITIONAL.

Trace mismatch. FR-052 is the default-module corpus inventory audit; FR-052-CON-3 does not exist. `properties` keys property shapes by obligation id at the quire boundary, which FR-052 never mentions, and it performs no inventory. The test asserts that keying, which is unrelated to the cited requirement: high per step-5.

`schema` lists ASSET_NAMES, returns a named asset's exact text, and refuses an unknown name as BadRequest (Outcome::Invalid, exit 2): every clause of FR-068-AC-8. The size ceiling is boundary hygiene. The test asserts byte-identity against the compiled-in constant, fully checking the clause it names; it does not reach the listing or refusal clauses (GAP-04 covers refusal), hence contested test_weaker / medium.

Same `schema` body as GAP-03, which implements AC-8's refusal clause. The test checks the BadRequest code, the op, the echoed name and that the known names are listed: the refusal clause it claims. It asserts the error code rather than the exit status 2 directly, and does not reach the byte-identity clause, hence contested test_weaker / medium.

`analyze_fan_out` collects obligations per suite in ordered sets, so duplicate bindings cannot raise obligation_count and rows come out sorted: AC-1 implemented. Unresolved-binding gaps are part of the report the FR statement names. The test's own claim is canonical-JSON rendering; it plants no duplicate symbol or duplicate (suite, obligation) entry, so AC-1's distinctive de-duplication claim is unasserted. Partial validation with the meaningful edge case unchecked: medium. (MP-233's targeted violating mutant for this triple survived the test, consistent with this label, but was not consulted to set it.)

The shown FR statement is the --relation clause: absent means the eight defaults, an explicit selection replaces them. `selected.map_or_else(defaults, |kinds| kinds)` does exactly that. Refusing a kind absent from the export vocabulary is input validation. The test checks absent -> default count and empty -> empty, the clause shown. AC-3's closure, cycle-termination and shortest-path clauses are not reached by this test, hence contested test_weaker / medium.

The shown FR statement: an absent or unreadable required path fails before row construction and names the failed input. `required` maps a read failure to InputUnreadable carrying `input`, before any GraphAnalysisInput exists; the premises and audit-identity checks are AC-9's own later clauses. The test removes audit.json and checks Refused, exit 2, input=audit and the QGA code: the clause shown. AC-9's retained-input-state clauses are not reached, hence contested test_weaker / medium.
